raw_answer_text:
A1: The four messages are DHCPDISCOVER, DHCPOFFER, DHCPREQUEST, and DHCPACK, in that order; the client sends the first one (DHCPDISCOVER).
A2: A server originates both the DHCPOFFER and the DHCPACK (in the drawn exchange, server B sends the DHCPACK).
A3: The DHCPACK message ("DHCPACK yiaddr=192.0.2.44") from the selected server moves the client into BOUND.
A4: The client moves into RENEWING state, and it addresses the DHCPREQUEST (unicast) to the server that originally issued its lease (server B).
A5: The client moves into REBINDING state, and the DHCPREQUEST it sends is broadcast (rather than unicast to the original server), so that any server may answer it.
A6: NOT STATED.
A7: A DHCPRELEASE message is sent by the client to give back/release its lease (the server side is captioned "Discards lease"); the RFC notes correct DHCP operation does not depend on it being sent.
A8: The client broadcasts a DHCPREQUEST naming the chosen server (server-id=B), so the server(s) not selected receive that same broadcast and read it as a declined offer, e.g. server A "may return 192.0.2.10 to the pool."
